sections.title: Macro
sections.content: Powell Day 2 Congressional testimony (Senate Banking). Day 1 (Jun 21) was hawkish - reiterated more hikes likely, inflation well above target. Fed paused Jun 14 at 5.00-5.25% but dot plot signals 2 more hikes in 2023. Markets partially digested hawkish message on Day 1. BoE rate decision due Jun 22 - surprise 50bp hike (vs 25bp expected) will ripple into US rate-sensitive sectors.

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.content: Titan submersible search ongoing (debris to be found Jun 22). Ukraine counteroffensive active. US-China relations stabilizing after Blinken visit Jun 18-19. No acute geopolitical shock.

sections.title: Earnings
sections.content: Accenture (ACN) reports before open Jun 22 - consensus expects solid results. KBH beat Q2 estimates after close Jun 21 - signals homebuilder strength. FedEx rallied on strong results Jun 20. Between major earnings seasons.

sections.title: SectorFlows
sections.content: Tech/AI rally extended but overbought. Homebuilders strong on new home demand. Financials mixed on rate outlook. Energy stable with WTI ~$72. Utilities and REITs under pressure from higher-for-longer rates.

sections.title: Technicals
sections.content: SPX ~4,366 at multi-month highs, extended rally. VIX compressed ~13-14 (complacent). 10Y yield ~3.73%. DXY ~102. Breadth narrow - mega-cap tech driving indices.

sections.title: Sentiment
sections.content: Bullish momentum but increasingly stretched. Low VIX suggests complacency. Powell Day 2 unlikely to add new hawkish shock (already priced from Day 1). BoE surprise could create intraday volatility in rate-sensitive names.

recommendations.thesis: KB Home beat Q2 earnings after close Jun 21 with strong orders and margins. Homebuilder sector has momentum. Gap-up expected at open. Entry on initial pullback from gap with target at prior resistance zone.
recommendations.catalyst: Post-earnings momentum, homebuilder sector strength, new home demand robust as existing inventory stays low
recommendations.risks: BoE 50bp surprise hike could briefly pressure rate-sensitive housing names; Powell Day 2 hawkish repeat

recommendations.thesis: Accenture reports before open Jun 22. Consensus expects solid IT consulting demand driven by AI/digital transformation spending. If results beat, stock should rally into AI narrative tailwind. Entry after initial reaction confirms positive.
recommendations.catalyst: Q3 earnings release before market open; AI consulting demand narrative
recommendations.risks: Miss on bookings or guidance could send it lower; entry only if earnings are positive
recommendations.conditional: ONLY enter if earnings reaction is positive. Skip if gap-down.

recommendations.thesis: AI momentum leader continues to attract flows. Any dip from Powell Day 2 or BoE noise is buyable in this regime. Stock has been consolidating after massive May earnings move. Looking for continuation pattern.
recommendations.catalyst: Persistent AI narrative, institutional FOMO, sector rotation into mega-cap tech on any macro uncertainty
recommendations.risks: Extended valuation, profit-taking risk at these levels, broad market pullback

recommendations.thesis: Homebuilder ETF benefits from KBH beat and existing home sales data due Jun 22. Low existing inventory continues to drive new home demand. Sector trend is strong.
recommendations.catalyst: KBH earnings beat spillover, existing home sales data, sector momentum
recommendations.risks: BoE surprise 50bp hike could temporarily weigh on rate-sensitive housing sector; Powell hawkish repeat

recommendations.thesis: BoE surprise 50bp hike (vs 25bp expected) will create global rate repricing pressure. Powell Day 2 reinforces higher-for-longer. Long-end Treasury prices should decline (yields rise). TLT is the cleanest expression of this view.
recommendations.catalyst: BoE 50bp surprise hike ripple effect, Powell Day 2 hawkish reinforcement, jobless claims data
recommendations.risks: Flight to safety if equity selloff intensifies; already partially priced after Powell Day 1

recommendations.thesis: Utilities sector is the classic rate-sensitive defensive play. BoE 50bp surprise and Powell hawkish Day 2 create a double headwind. Higher rates reduce the relative attractiveness of utility dividends. Range-bound regime with negative bias favors this short.
recommendations.catalyst: BoE surprise hike global rate repricing, Powell testimony reinforcement, rotation out of defensives into growth/AI
recommendations.risks: Broad market selloff could trigger flight to defensives; oversold bounce
